summary: Plan sampling, interpret workplace exposure results, and verify controls across key hazards. Explore this practical occupational hygiene course.
lede: Occupational exposure assessment helps workplace health and safety professionals plan representative sampling and use findings to guide controls. Designed for industrial hygienists, occupational health practitioners, and safety managers, the course covers chemical and dust sampling, noise, heat, vibration, and biological-agent assessment, along with interpreting results against applicable criteria. Practical exercises include checking controls, linking findings with incident and health-surveillance processes, and prioritizing corrective actions while considering data quality and privacy.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess or manage worker exposure and need to turn field observations, measurements, and health information into defensible control actions. This course is designed for: Industrial hygienists planning personal and area exposure sampling. Occupational health practitioners linking exposure findings with health-surveillance processes. Safety managers integrating hygiene findings into ISO 45001 risk controls. Environmental-health officers assessing workplace agents and documenting exposure concerns. Mine health and safety managers prioritizing dust, noise, heat, and vibration controls. Factory managers coordinating production controls with chemical and noise assessments. Construction HSE managers planning task-based exposure checks across changing worksites. Energy and utilities occupational hygiene specialists reviewing field-worker exposure profiles. HR health-team leads coordinating psychosocial risk evidence and worker-support processes. HSE auditors checking sampling records, exposure actions, and control-verification evidence.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with workplace health and safety processes or occupational health is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring examples of workplace tasks or exposure concerns if available; remove personal or confidential health information before use. Instrument demonstrations and hands-on measurement activities depend on equipment availability and delivery arrangements. Advanced instrument methods and AI-assisted prioritization are covered at conceptual or operational awareness level, not as technical implementation.
